text:
maya: quick heads-up — i'm planning to add a schema lint rule to the model config validator that will fail if a config doesn't include either `max_seq_len` or `tokenizer.max_length`. we've seen a couple of models defaulting to 2048 unexpectedly and causing OOMs.
chad: ok good call. will that break all existing models without the field?
maya: it will fail the lint in CI, but won't block runtime. the plan is: lint failure -> require explicit opt-in via `compatibility.legacy=true` or adding defaults in onboarding. we need to decide the sane default for most of our catalog.
lin: for the open models we usually assume 2048, but for finetuned small-context models it's often 1024. maybe the validator could check weights metadata (if present) for config hints before failing?
maya: yeah, i can add a heuristic: if weights metadata has `max_ctx`/`n_ctx` use that; else lint fail. also add a message suggesting `tokenizer.max_length` or `max_seq_len`.
olga: +1 on the heuristic. also we should catch mismatches between `tokenizer.name` and the tokenizer files in S3 (e.g., vocab.json vs tokenizer.json). ran into that with the chinese-qa model.
maya: good point — i'll add a quick check that lists files under the model path and compares to tokenizer.type mapping. example: if tokenizer.name=="sentencepiece" expect .model file.
deploy-bot: [deploy-check] config-lint job started for PR #2412
sam: is there an RFC for how we treat missing fields vs explicit defaults? i remember we debated implicit defaulting last quarter.
maya: no formal RFC yet. i can draft one. minimal proposal: reject missing critical fields in the onboarding validator; allow runtime defaults only when `compatibility.allow_runtime_defaults=true` in the model's config (explicit opt-in). this makes the onboarding process explicit.
chad: sounds reasonable. acceptance criteria?
maya: 1) validator lint rule that fails in CI if `max_seq_len` and `tokenizer.max_length` both absent and no weights metadata hint. 2) helpful error message with remediation steps and a docs link. 3) a migration script we can run to add `compatibility.legacy=true` for models we want to keep working immediately. 4) unit tests + integration smoke test that runs on a small sample of models.
lin: for the docs link include examples for common tokenizers and the expected files. also add an example `config.json` snippet:

```
{
  "model": "my-cool-model",
  "tokenizer": {
    "name": "sentencepiece",
    "vocab_path": "s3://models/my-cool-model/tokenizer.model",
    "max_length": 1024
  },
  "max_seq_len": 1024,
  "compatibility": {
    "legacy": false
  }
}
```

olga: +1 on the snippet. also can we add a lint warning (not fail) for `tokenizer.truncate_strategy` not set? we've had truncation surprises.
maya: yes i'll add a warning for truncate_strategy and pad_side. we should be careful about warning fatigue though.
ci-bot: config-lint | PR #2412 | tests: unit(✓) integration(✗)
sam: integration failed — what's flaking?
maya: looks like the new rule caught a batch of older models in `s3://models/legacy/` that lack fields. i'm going to push a matcher to exclude `models/legacy/` for now and file a migration ticket.
chad: please add the exclusion as a temporary allowlist and link the migration ticket in the PR description.
maya: will do. PR link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/2412 — reviewers: @chad @lin @olga
lin: quick note: when you add the weights metadata heuristic, please make it permissive — check both `n_ctx` and `max_ctx` keys and tolerate strings/ints.
maya: noted. i'll add normalization in the validator: try int(value) else parse digits from string.
olga: can we also log a telemetry event when a model is flagged by the lint so product can prioritize migration list?
maya: yep — add telemetry event `config_lint_flagged` with tags: model_name, reason, account_id.
ci-bot: config-lint | PR #2412 | tests: integration(✓)
deploy-bot: [deploy-check] merges blocked until lint rules merged
sam: thanks maya — will review today. after this lands, we should run the migration script on staging models first.
maya: agreed. i'll open the migration ticket and add a small playbook in the PR describing the staged run (staging -> subset prod -> full prod). ping me for the run.
chad: noted. thx.
olga: thanks, this will reduce weird OOM incidents.
maya: thanks everyone. closing loop — i'll merge after addressing review comments and adding the migration ticket.
